A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrochetBench with the same authors, benchmark, and four-task framework. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the main text, figures, tables, and appendices, including material moved or renumbered.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of nine models, supervised finetuning, execution outcomes, and dataset analyses in Table 2, Figures 3–5, and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and reports revised project-level results, a parsing-fidelity audit, and BERTScore results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o-mini parsing pipeline, four-task framework, CrochetPARADE execution procedure, evaluation prompts, and supervised finetuning approach remain substantively unchanged. Additional training and annotation details do not establish a changed algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the Yarnspirations corpus of 6,085 patterns across 55 categories and the same four tasks. The revised project-level sample size and partitions concern existing coverage; the added audits do not introduce another domain, population, or task scenario.

E2.justification: The same nine base models and finetuned Qwen2-VL comparison remain in corresponding experiments. The new BERTScore table evaluates existing models under an additional metric without changing comparator membership in the retained comparisons.

E3.justification: v2 specifies 100 project-level Task D items; v3 specifies 6,009 dataset items and held-out evaluation using a shared, pattern-level 80/5/15 split for Tasks A–C and project-level D. Table 1 changes 'Test Size' to 'Dataset Size'; the 119-item step-level test remains. This substantially revises the reported evaluation design without establishing which experiments were rerun. v3 also introduces a 494-pattern parsing audit and BERTScore evaluation.

E4.justification: v3 adds focused analyses of parsing fidelity through overlap measurements and manual inspection, and of BERTScore concentration in Appendix D. Appendix B removes the project-type-by-skill breakdown and rare-label complexity details. The existing step-depth analysis, error taxonomy, and star-pattern case study remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added parsing-overlap range and BERTScore point estimates do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Project-level results change substantially: Figure 4 reports Qwen2-VL-7B validity of 21.0% versus 39.5%, and GPT-4o undefined-stitch errors of 29.0% versus 70.3%. Figure 5 changes Gemini DINO similarity from 0.115 to 0.215. These are revised results under changed reported settings, not established same-setting gains. v3 adds parsing-fidelity and BERTScore results and removes granular appendix statistics. Table 2 and Figure 3 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The DSL descriptions and existing metric definitions remain substantively unchanged. Neither version develops theoretical propositions or proofs, and the added BERTScore analysis introduces no formal derivation or mathematical result.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the same four-task executable crochet benchmark and a persistent gap between recognition and procedural synthesis despite scaling and finetuning. The finetuning statement added to v3's conclusion already appears in v2's introduction and experiments.

C2.justification: v3 attributes smaller models' relatively high project-level validity to copying few-shot exemplars, explains BERTScore concentration through templated language, and explicitly acknowledges uncontrolled overlap with pretraining corpora. It also explains the annotation burden behind the small step-level set. These add substantive qualifications without replacing the overall interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies typical 2000-by-2000 sRGB images, line-by-line annotation verification, and Qwen2-VL-7B-Instruct finetuning with AdamW, three epochs, and effective batch size eight. It drops v2's explicit full-parameter-update statement. The advertised code location changes from an anonymous repository to a named GitHub repository, and the ethics section reports copyright-holder permission.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to BERTScore, research on visually grounded models' classification weaknesses, Cheffusion, and ChemHGNN. These supplement metric justification and contextual positioning while retaining the central relationship to descriptive benchmarks and executable program synthesis. Publication and bibliography corrections do not constitute new research coverage.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites parts of the dataset and ethics descriptions, adds explanatory passages, simplifies Appendix B's subsection structure, corrects the finetuning table reference, and edits the author header. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset throughout. Figure 1 receives a higher-resolution replacement, and Figures 3–5 change typography, legends, or axes, including Figure 5's vertical range from 0–0.7 to 0–1.0. Appendix tables move closer to their discussion; some statistical displays are removed or consolidated, and the BERTScore table is added. Figures 2 and 8 retain their imagery.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, v3 provides useful parsing-fidelity evidence, metric analysis, clearer evaluation and training documentation, and an explicit pretraining-overlap limitation. These improve the benchmark's auditability and outweigh the limited loss of granular dataset statistics. The improvement remains modest because reporting inconsistencies persist: for example, v3 states 42.4% undefined-stitch errors for Gemma-3-27B while Figure 4 shows 43.4%. Higher revised scores alone do not establish improved paper quality.
